basis: Proline-biosynthesis disorder with defining cutis laxa and intellectual disability; osteopenia 10/11 and hip dislocation 15/22. Cataract 2/22; glaucoma evidence limited to singletons.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: PYCR1 deficiency is an inborn disorder of proline biosynthesis, supporting the metabolic mechanism axis.

basis: Temple syndrome is defined by growth and endocrine abnormalities with characteristic infantile hypotonia and developmental impairment; small hands and feet alone do not establish skeletal damage.

decisions.neurologic: primary: characteristic infantile hypotonia and developmental impairment form part of the defining Temple syndrome phenotype.

basis: Extensive myelomeningocele directly involves spinal neural tissue and vertebral closure. Neurogenic bladder is separately diagnosed; urinary tract damage is not established by this record.

decisions.renal: none: neurogenic bladder is a separately diagnosed consequence of spinal dysfunction; its frequency does not establish direct urinary tract damage.

basis: Inherited coagulation deficiency; cerebral hemorrhage and joint/intramuscular hemorrhage are each annotated frequent (30-79%), supporting direct brain and musculoskeletal injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: joint and intramuscular hemorrhage are direct tissue injuries, each annotated frequent (30-79%); these exceed superficial bruising.

basis: Familial primary myelofibrosis affects marrow and blood; hepatic extramedullary hematopoietic infiltration occurs in roughly 40%. Splenic disease remains within haematologic.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic extramedullary hematopoiesis represents direct clonal infiltration/occupation in roughly 40% of primary myelofibrosis patients.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disorder with defining developmental impairment and structural CNS abnormalities. Muscle enzyme deficiency alone does not establish myopathy; hepatic frequency is unknown.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: respiratory-chain deficiency in a muscle sample does not establish damaging myopathy; axial hypotonia can arise from the defining CNS disease.

basis: Pontocerebellar hypoplasia and prenatal contractures define PCH4; contractures occur in 2/4. Central apnea and neurogenic dysphagia do not establish lung or gastrointestinal injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: prenatal contractures are explicitly part of the disease definition, supported by contractures in 2/4 and frequent arthrogryposis.

basis: Cerebellar degeneration and peripheral neuropathy define AOA4. Oculomotor apraxia is neurologic; hypercholesterolemia in 5/9 is a biochemical feature without demonstrated additional organ injury.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: hypercholesterolemia in 5/9 is characteristic, but does not by itself establish direct endocrine injury or a damaging metabolic disorder within AOA4.

basis: Gluconeogenesis disorder with hypoglycemia and a classic hepatic steatosis/failure phenotype; quantitative frequencies are unavailable. Renal steatosis alone does not establish kidney dysfunction.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatic steatosis and liver failure characterize the classic reported hepatometabolic presentation; precise frequencies are unavailable.

basis: Complex I metabolic deficiency; developmental impairment/cerebellar atrophy and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy each reported in 1/1 assessed. Tiny samples limit certainty; optic atrophy 1-4% excluded.

decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental impairment and cerebellar atrophy demonstrate direct CNS involvement in 1/1 assessed; the defining disorder is complex I metabolic deficiency.
